Alyssa — good call on the medication-normalization risk. Below are the recommended candidates and the concise trade study for quantization options we plan to run in the pilot. I'm keeping the note high-level and actionable so procurement can see the tech choices.

Candidate models (hosted variants):
- Redwood-7B-v2 (float16) — baseline for quality; expected dev accuracy on our clinical extraction eval ~94.5% (unquantized).
- LlamaX-13B-ptq (GPTQ) — good mid/large model tradeoff; slightly higher latency, expected accuracy ~93.8% when run with conservative PTQ.
- Phoenix-6B-awq (AWQ-optimized) — smallest memory footprint, excellent throughput; expected accuracy ~92.0–93.0% with AWQ profiles.

Quantization options we will validate (pilot experiments):
- AWQ (Aggressive Weight Quantization): smallest memory and best throughput; risk: narrow degradation on tokens requiring fine-grained numeric fidelity (med names/dosages). We'll run field-level accuracy checks and targeted prompts for medication normalization.
- GPTQ/PTQ: better quality retention than aggressive AWQ for many architectures; slightly higher VRAM and slower single-request latency. Good middle ground for larger models (13B).
- FP8 mixed-precision: where supported on our Dedicated runtime, FP8 can preserve most float16-quality characteristics while lowering memory and sometimes improving throughput. Hardware support is limited and adds deployment complexity.

Planned pilot experiments (each on the same 10k record subset):
1) Baseline: Redwood-7B float16 (no quant) — metric: field-level accuracy, latency, token cost.
2) AWQ on Phoenix-6B — measure regressions on medication normalization + throughput gains.
3) GPTQ on LlamaX-13B — conservative PTQ profile; measure quality vs latency/cost.
4) FP8 variant on Redwood-7B (if we can provision runtime) — compare to float16 baseline.

Deliverables and acceptance criteria:
- Benchmarks (CSV + dashboard link) for latency/throughput/cost per model+quant profile.
- A short regression report highlighting fields that drop >2% absolute accuracy, with examples and root-cause hypotheses.
- Recommended pilot winner + suggested Dedicated sizing and expected monthly cost estimate.

Attachments I'll share after the run: a short table with expected p50/p95 latency gaps and an initial risk matrix. In the meantime, here's a short benchmark link for the small synthetic run we did earlier: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cNexteraBenchmarks

If procurement needs a draft MAA/SOW, Ben can share a templated SOW we usually use for 2-week discovery pilots.

— Soojin
